name: Naproxen Sodium + Domperidone
meta: Naproxen Sodium: NSAID (propionic acid derivative); Domperidone: Peripheral dopamine D2 antagonist (prokinetic / antiemetic)
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Naproxen Sodium: Schedule
H – prescription only; Domperidone: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: 230.26 g/mol (acid); 252.24 g/mol (sodium; 550 mg sodium ≈ 500 mg naproxen)
White crystalline powder; sodium salt soluble in water.
White or almost white powder, practically insoluble in water.

Naproxen Sodium: A propionic acid NSAID; the sodium salt gives faster absorption, useful in acute pain and migraine. First approval/introduction: Patented 1967; first marketed 1976 (Syntex). Domperidone: In 2014 the EMA restricted use to relief of nausea and vomiting at a maximum of 10 mg three times daily, generally for ≤1 week, because of cardiac risks. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1974 (Janssen Pharmaceutica); marketed 1979 (Switzerland, West Germany); not approved in the USA.
Migraine causes gastric stasis that delays drug absorption. Domperidone restores gastric motility and controls nausea, enhancing naproxen absorption and onset of analgesia.

Naproxen Sodium Non-selective COX inhibitor; reduces prostaglandin-mediated neurogenic inflammation in migraine and musculoskeletal pain. Receptor / target profile: Non-selective reversible COX-1 and COX-2 inhibitor.

Domperidone Blocks peripheral D2 receptors in the upper GI tract (increasing oesophageal sphincter tone and gastric emptying) and in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (outside the blood–brain barrier). Receptor / target profile: Peripherally selective D2 and D3 antagonist; acts on the chemoreceptor trigger zone (outside the blood–brain barrier) and upper GI tract; raises prolactin.
Summary: Sodium salt rapidly absorbed; Tmax ~1 h. >99% protein bound. Half-life 12–17 h.
Summary: Bioavailability ~15% (first-pass); Tmax ~1 h (SR prolonged). ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life 7–9 h.
Acute treatment of migraine attacks with or without aura, particularly with nausea/vomiting
One tablet at onset of migraine; a second tablet may be taken after 8–12 h if required
Maximum 2 tablets in 24 h; not for prophylaxis
Not recommended in children and patients >60 years with cardiac risk
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Avoid in severe impairment (CrCl <30); monitor creatinine in mild–moderate impairment.
Avoid in severe impairment; use lowest dose in mild–moderate.
Higher risk of GI bleeding, renal impairment and CV events – lowest dose, shortest time; consider gastroprotection (PPI).
Severe: reduce frequency to once or twice daily.
>60 years: higher arrhythmia risk – use lowest dose.
≥12 years and ≥35 kg: adult dosing; younger: 0.25 mg/kg up to three times daily (specialist).
Excreted in small amounts; use with caution.
Hypersensitivity, or asthma/urticaria/rhinitis triggered by aspirin or other NSAIDs
Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding; history of recurrent ulceration
Known QT prolongation, significant electrolyte disturbance, underlying cardiac disease (e.g. heart failure)
Concomitant QT-prolonging drugs or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
Cardiovascular thrombotic events (MI, stroke) – use lowest dose for shortest time
GI ulceration, bleeding and perforation – higher risk in elderly, with steroids, anticoagulants, SSRIs
Hepatotoxicity – monitor LFTs on long-term use
Serious ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death – risk higher >60 years and >30 mg/day; use lowest dose, max ~1 week
Raised prolactin – galactorrhoea, gynaecomastia, menstrual irregularity
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics (reduced effect, renal impairment)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) – contraindicated
Naproxen Sodium: Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Naproxen Sodium: BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.
Domperidone: ECG if cardiac risk factors; potassium, magnesium.
Naproxen Sodium: GI bleeding, renal impairment, seizures; supportive care. Domperidone: Drowsiness, disorientation, EPS (especially children), arrhythmias. ECG monitoring; supportive care.
Naproxen sodium is effective for acute migraine (Cochrane, Law et al., 2013); domperidone reduces migraine-associated gastric stasis and nausea.
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Use for the shortest time (usually ≤1 week)
Inform doctor of all heart medicines and antifungals/antibiotics
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
